_doc: P4 set for work/2026-08-08-east-pipeline: species the LoRA has NEVER seen.
Kept separate from eval_east.json on purpose (its _untrained_note): iou_ref is UNDEFINED here
because no real sprite exists, so these rows cannot share the trained set's scoring contract.
Mixing them would invite averaging over the undefined half.
Verified absent from BOTH lora_eval.SRC and the silhouette bank. The judges here are the
structural gate, the interior metrics, and the eye.
anteater   NO close body plan - long snout, bushy tail, low body. The predecessor's
generalisation precedent, and the sharpest test of a style-only LoRA.
armadillo  NO close body plan - armoured, compact, short-legged.
okapi      HAS a close plan (equine/deer). The easy case; if this fails, nothing works.
warthog    HAS a close plan (pig). Tusks and a heavy head the family rep lacks.

subjects.why: no close corpus body plan; nearest family rep is Bear and it is a poor fit
no close corpus body plan; nearest family rep is Pig, armour and proportions differ
close plan (Pig) but with tusks and a heavier head

S2a.why: the only measured method that can serve an untrained species - S1 needs a corpus sprite that does not exist

S0.why: the incumbent wolf template, as the floor

S1n.why: S1 is UNDEFINED for an untrained species (no corpus sprite of its own). The honest analogue is a HAND-PICKED nearest corpus species - which is what a human would do, and it tests how much the choice of neighbour is worth.
